name: Translational Research in Affective Disorders Lab
piOverview: Michael Treadway is a cognitive neuroscientist and clinical psychologist who studies motivation and the brain systems involved in weighing costs and benefits.
researchOverview: The TReAD Lab investigates how changes in reward circuitry contribute to motivational difficulties in depression and other affective disorders, including the roles of stress and immune function. Its work combines computational models, brain imaging, assessments of daily experience, and experimental interventions to identify mechanisms that could inform treatment.

name: Computational Mechanisms of Psychopathology Lab
piOverview: Vanessa Brown is a clinical scientist whose research examines learning and decision-making in anxiety, trauma-related conditions, and depression, with an emphasis on processes relevant to treatment.
researchOverview: The COMP Lab uses computational models to study how people learn under uncertainty and how these processes change with psychological difficulties and treatment. Behavioral tasks, neuroimaging, real-world assessments, and interventions help connect formal theories of learning to clinically meaningful questions, including whether computational measures are reliable and useful in practice.

name: The Translational Lab
piOverview: Pete Hitchcock combines training in clinical psychology and behavioral treatment with computational research on learning and choice in depression and anxiety.
researchOverview: The Translational Lab studies how emotions, beliefs, and context shape decisions, including the processes underlying rumination and worry. Carefully designed behavioral experiments and models of learning and evidence accumulation support its broader aim: translating decision science into precise, scalable psychological interventions, including self-guided treatments.

name: Developmental Personality Neuroscience Lab
piOverview: Michael Hallquist studies the brain and behavioral processes underlying personality, emotional instability, and self-regulation, with particular attention to adolescence and young adulthood.
researchOverview: The DEPENd Lab examines how emotions and social cues interact with reward learning and goal-directed decisions. Computational models, functional neuroimaging, and assessments of daily experience help explain individual differences in impulsivity and interpersonal difficulties. The lab also shares training resources in quantitative methods and reproducible data analysis.

name: Emotion Cognition and Computation Lab
piOverview: Philip Kragel studies how the brain gives rise to cognition and emotion, combining psychology, neuroscience, and machine learning to understand what distinguishes different mental processes.
researchOverview: The ECCO Lab develops biologically grounded models of cognition and emotion using functional neuroimaging, physiological recordings, and computational models of behavior. Its work links neural networks and other quantitative models to human brain activity, with an emphasis on predictions that can be tested across independent studies and laboratories.

name: Learning, Understanding, Memory, & Neurodevelopment Lab
piOverview: Ali Cohen is a developmental cognitive neuroscientist who studies how emotion and motivation shape learning and memory from childhood through adulthood.
researchOverview: The LUMeN Lab investigates the brain and cognitive mechanisms through which motivationally salient experiences become lasting memories and guide future behavior across development. Its work combines behavioral paradigms, neuroimaging, psychophysiology, and computational modeling to examine reward, emotion, and the complexity of learning environments across age.
